secondary_source_scope: User-provided Austrian WHT summary sections 7.3.4.1 to 7.3.4.5

claims.secondary_source_claim: Corporate dividend withholding can be reduced to the corporate rate from 2024.
claims.current_rule: For qualifying capital income of a corporate KESt debtor, § 93 Abs. 1a permits 23% withholding for income from 2024 onward; this is distinct from the general 27.5% capital-income rate.
claims.decision_impact: Use 23% only on the corporate-recipient domestic baseline route; do not hard-code 27.5% for corporate dividends.

claims.secondary_source_claim: EU parent-company relief requires qualifying EU status, at least 10% participation and a continuous one-year holding period.
claims.current_rule: Current § 94 Z 2 provides the qualifying EU-parent relief with a one-tenth participation and uninterrupted one-year holding requirement, subject to statutory anti-abuse / hidden-distribution restrictions.
claims.decision_impact: Domestic § 94 relief is evaluated before treaty relief and is represented as a non-rate exemption treatment.

claims.secondary_source_claim: If the one-year holding period is not complete at payment, withholding is provisional and relief may later be obtained by refund.
claims.current_rule: Immediate § 94 Z 2 relief is unavailable before the one-year period is complete. Austrian guidance/case material confirms withholding, potentially at a treaty-reduced level, followed by a refund claim after the holding condition is met.
claims.decision_impact: Do not output 0% at payment merely because eventual directive relief is expected. Continue treaty analysis to determine the interim withholding amount.

claims.secondary_source_claim: Anti-abuse / hidden-distribution circumstances may block immediate source exemption and require withholding/refund treatment.
claims.current_rule: Current § 94 Z 2 expressly preserves withholding in specified abuse/hidden-distribution circumstances; any later directive-compliant refund is a separate state requiring factual review.
claims.decision_impact: Source-relief eligibility and substantive/refund eligibility are separate review fields.

claims.secondary_source_claim: Portfolio corporate recipients can in defined cases obtain a refund where Austrian WHT cannot be credited in the residence state; third-country relief is possible with extensive administrative assistance and a sub-10% holding.
claims.current_rule: § 21 Abs. 1 Z 1a KStG provides a refund remedy subject to residence/administrative-assistance and non-creditability conditions; it is not an exemption at source.
claims.decision_impact: Never convert § 21 KStG refund eligibility into a 0% payment-date WHT result.

claims.secondary_source_claim: Austrian-source interest of a non-resident company without an Austrian PE is generally exempt subject to a four-part written declaration.
claims.current_rule: Current § 98 Abs. 1 Z 5 excludes interest not received by natural persons from Austrian limited tax liability. The older four-part declaration description is not used as the general current corporate-interest eligibility gate. Special § 99 categories still require separate classification.
claims.decision_impact: For an ordinary corporate recipient, current domestic no-WHT treatment is resolved under § 98 before treaty analysis; special interest categories remain fail-closed.

claims.secondary_source_claim: Royalties within the Austrian statutory royalty route are generally subject to 20% withholding.
claims.current_rule: § 99 Abs. 1 Z 3 together with § 100 provides the 20% gross-basis withholding route, but only after the payment is classified within the relevant rights-exploitation/source nexus.
claims.decision_impact: 20% is not a generic rate for every payment labelled royalty and technical/commercial consulting must not leak into this classifier.

claims.secondary_source_claim: Eligible EU/EEA recipients may deduct expenses at withholding stage and the WHT rate is 25%; expenses above EUR 2,000 require additional security of domestic taxation.
claims.current_rule: Current § 99 Abs. 2 Z 2 allows directly related expenses for an EU/EEA limited taxpayer if disclosed in writing before payment. The current statutory security threshold is EUR 2,463. Under § 100 Abs. 1a Z 1 a corporate recipient uses 23% from 2024 on the net-after-admissible-expenses base. For non-corporate recipients, § 100 Abs. 1 uses 20% up to EUR 20,000 annual income and 25% on the excess.
claims.decision_impact: The review model must record both rate and tax base. A 20% gross route and 23% corporate net route must never be compared as if they applied to the same base.

claims.secondary_source_claim: The Interest and Royalties Directive relief requires beneficial ownership, qualifying EU entities, 25% association and a continuous one-year holding period; withholding/refund applies where the holding period is incomplete.
claims.current_rule: Current § 99a confirms beneficial ownership, qualifying entity/tax conditions, a 25% direct relationship in either direction or common-parent alternative, one-year holding, documentary confirmations at payment, a statutory refund route where holding/documentation is missing, and exclusions for profit-participating claims, abuse and non-arm's-length excess.
claims.decision_impact: Substantive § 99a eligibility, documentation at payment, immediate source relief and later refund are separate decision states.

claims.secondary_source_claim: A special EU-Switzerland agreement can exempt qualifying intercompany dividends, interest and royalties, while more favourable treaty provisions remain available.
claims.current_rule: The former Article 15 was retained and renumbered Article 9. Current Article 9 generally requires a direct 25% relationship and two-year holding for dividends; for interest/royalties it requires a 25% direct association or common-parent relationship for two years, plus residence, entity/tax and anti-abuse conditions. More favourable DTT treatment remains unaffected.
claims.decision_impact: For CH, create a parallel Article 9 international-relief candidate and compare it with the applicable DTT; do not silently replace the DTT route.

claims.secondary_source_claim: Treaty relief may be available at source or through refund and documentary requirements such as residence confirmation apply.
claims.current_rule: The DBA-Entlastungsverordnung permits relief at source under its conditions; its use is optional for the Austrian payer. Current BMF materials continue to use ZS-QU1/ZS-QU2 for residence/treaty entitlement evidence, with simplified documentation in qualifying low-value cases. Failure to use or qualify for source relief does not destroy substantive treaty entitlement and may lead to a refund route.
claims.decision_impact: Treaty rate and payment-date withholding rate are separate outputs; documentary readiness is a reviewer fact.

claims.secondary_source_claim: FASTER must be transposed by 31 December 2028 and applies from 1 January 2030.
claims.current_rule: Council Directive (EU) 2025/50 Article 25 requires transposition by 31 December 2028 and application from 1 January 2030.
claims.decision_impact: FASTER is displayed only as future-law context and must not alter a 2026 AT result.

claims.secondary_source_claim: Technical/commercial consulting and supervisory-board payments can have separate Austrian withholding rules.
claims.current_rule: These are distinct statutory categories from the product's current dividend/interest/royalty scope.
claims.decision_impact: Do not add a new public transaction type in this workstream; use the finding as a semantic guard preventing consulting/service percentages from being classified as royalty rates.
